column2: The exact date and time the record was created on the device (in ISO 8601 format).
The precise Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) provided by the GPS satellites, used for global time synchronization.
The north/south geographic coordinate of the device.
The east/west geographic coordinate of the device.
The current speed of the vehicle in kilometers per hour.
The compass direction (0-360 degrees) the vehicle is traveling.
The elevation of the device above sea level, measured in meters.
The number of GPS satellites the device is currently locked onto. A higher number generally means better location accuracy.
Horizontal Dilution of Precision. This is a measure of GPS accuracy. A lower value (typically 1 or 2) indicates high precision, while a higher value indicates lower accuracy.
The distance (in meters) of the segment or between points.
The cumulative distance (in meters) traveled since the start of the recording session.
These represent the readings from the device's Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), which detects vibrations caused by road roughness.
The calculated International Roughness Index. If 0, the vehicle is stationary or the processing engine has not yet begun reporting roughness.
A categorical label (e.g., "D") representing the road surface condition based on the IRI value.
A numerical score reflecting the reliability of the IRI calculation.
A letter grade (e.g., "F") summarizing the confidence in the measurement.
The sampling frequency of your sensors, measured in Hertz (Hz). e.g., 100 means the device is capturing 100 sensor readings every second.
